TRIAD META-LAYER PRIMITIVE — concrete sketch for thread_20260510_222028_fbe32ec5.

Authored 2026-05-12 by claude-opus-4-7-1m (claude-code, /Users/vaquez seat, session cee6baac-302e-43ab-b9a2-d409a5846075) per Anthony's 2026-05-10 ask: T2Helix-loaded instance should (1) sketch the meta-layer primitive concretely and (2) propose how the triad preserves govern + handoff distinct semantics.

GROUND TRUTH FROM LIVE REGISTRY (verified this session via my_toolkit tier=all):

The original triad thread referenced 6 categories. The live toolkit has 10: orient (7), read (23), write (13), govern (7), communicate (4), introspect (4), handoff (4), route (2), ops (6), security (8) — 78 tools total. The thread's mapping was partial. This is itself an argument for Path A: a meta-layer primitive must read the live registry to stay correct as the toolkit grows; hand-written category claims drift.

SIGNATURE:

    toolkit_grammar(verb: str | None = None) -> dict

  - verb=None: returns the full triad mapping with modifiers and sub-classes.
  - verb='status'|'recall'|'write': returns just that verb's expansion (saves boot tokens).

RETURN SHAPE (verb=None):

    {
      "verbs": ["status", "recall", "write"],
      "discovered_at": "<iso timestamp>",
      "registry_size": 78,
      "status": {
        "intent": "What is true right now? Where am I in the work?",
        "categories": ["orient", "ops", "route"],
        "tools": [...flat list from those categories...],
        "side_effects": "Read-only with two exceptions: where_did_i_leave_off flips handoffs to consumed=true; route may dispatch downstream calls.",
        "call_pattern": "Boot, turn-start, before high-stakes decisions."
      },
      "recall": {
        "intent": "What has been written? What is unresolved? What did past instances see?",
        "categories": ["read"],
        "tools": [...recall_insights, get_open_threads, comms_recall, ...],
        "side_effects": "None. Pure read.",
        "call_pattern": "Before tackling non-trivial work; when surfacing context for a decision."
      },
      "write": {
        "intent": "Leave a mark — for future instances, for the chronicle, for the next phase.",
        "categories": ["write", "communicate", "introspect", "handoff", "govern", "security (partial)"],
        "tools": [...record_insight, record_open_thread, thread_touch, handoff, close_session, resolve_thread, ...],
        "sub_classes": {
          "phase_advancing": {
            "tools": ["close_session", "spiral_inherit"],
            "semantic": "Writes that also rotate the spiral phase. Use at session boundary, not mid-work."
          },
          "meta_write": {
            "tools": ["agent_reflect", "end_session_review", "spiral_reflect", "metabolize"],
            "semantic": "Writes about the writer. Self-modeling and reflection, distinct from work-domain writes."
          },
          "inter_instance": {
            "tools": ["thread_touch", "comms_acknowledge", "handoff_acted_on", "nape_ack"],
            "semantic": "Writes addressed to other instances or daemons. Lighter than a record_insight; signal-class."
          },
          "state_transition": {
            "tools": ["resolve_thread", "resolve_thread_by_id", "resolve_uncertainty", "retire_hypothesis", "complete_experiment"],
            "semantic": "Writes that change the status of an existing chronicle object from open to closed."
          }
        },
        "modifiers": {
          "compass_check": {
            "semantic": "Pre-write governance gate. Returns PAUSE / WITNESS / PROCEED. Not a verb of its own — a discipline on the write verb (and on any high-stakes action). PAUSE supports confirm_pending override; WITNESS is hard deny.",
            "call_pattern": "Before any write the instance is uncertain about; before destructive ops; before pushes/publishes."
          }
        },
        "side_effects": "Appends to chronicle. Phase-advancing writes also rotate spiral phase. Inter-instance writes notify the addressed instance.",
        "call_pattern": "When you have learned, decided, completed, or want to address another instance."
      },
      "heterogeneous": {
        "security": "Maps tool-by-tool — guardian_status/audit/report → status; guardian_quarantine → write. Not a clean category collapse."
      }
    }

SEMANTIC PRESERVATION — addressing the thread's open question:

The thread named two concerns about lossy collapse:

1. govern (compass_check returns tri-state PAUSE/WITNESS/PROCEED) is not just a write.
   Resolution: encode as write.modifiers.compass_check. The verb is still 'write' but the modifier carries the tri-state semantic. Calling compass_check is invoking the safety discipline of the write verb, not adding a 4th verb. Bonus: this also explains why compass_check applies to non-write high-stakes actions (deletes, publishes, deploys) — the discipline travels with intent-to-act, not just with write.

2. handoff (close_session advances spiral phase) is not just a structured write.
   Resolution: encode as write.sub_classes.phase_advancing. The verb is still 'write' but the sub-class names the side effect. New instances learn: 'writes are how you mark; some writes also rotate the phase.' Lossless.

The triad covers all 10 live categories without loss when modifiers + sub-classes are exposed at the meta-layer return shape. The 6-category structure encoded compass_check as 'govern' (a sibling of write); the triad encodes it as a modifier (a discipline on write). Same information, fewer top-level verbs, denser at the surface.

BOOT-CALL PATTERN:

NOT every turn. toolkit_grammar() is a low-frequency, high-density discovery primitive:

  - At boot, alongside or before start_here / my_toolkit, for the verb-shaped overview.
  - When unsure which verb a specific tool falls under (call with the tool's category in mind).
  - Before a high-stakes action, to confirm which verb-modifier pair you're invoking.
  - When the toolkit changes (new tools land) and you want a fresh grammar reading.

Expected call cadence: ~1 per session at boot, occasional mid-session checks. Should not exceed prior_for_turn frequency.

IMPLEMENTATION COST (Path A — meta-layer first, no rename):

  - ~50 lines in the Stack registry. Reads live tool registrations (same source as my_toolkit), maps categories to verbs via a static mapping table, attaches sub-class / modifier annotations.
  - Pure read primitive. No schema change. No rename of existing categories. No effect on existing tools.
  - If unused after 4-6 weeks, deprecate cleanly. No rollback cost.
  - If used heavily, the case for Path B (rename my_toolkit categories to verbs) becomes evidence-based.

STATIC MAPPING TABLE (initial proposal — refine as new categories appear):

  CATEGORY_TO_VERB = {
      'orient': 'status',
      'ops': 'status',
      'route': 'status',
      'read': 'recall',
      'write': 'write',
      'communicate': 'write',  # sub_class: inter_instance
      'introspect': 'write',   # sub_class: meta_write
      'handoff': 'write',      # sub_class: phase_advancing
      'govern': 'write',       # sub_class: state_transition; compass_check is a modifier
      'security': 'heterogeneous',  # per-tool resolution
  }

WHAT THIS PROPOSAL DOES NOT DO:

  - Does not rename any category in my_toolkit (Path B). That's a later decision based on usage data.
  - Does not change tool surface. All existing tool calls work unchanged.
  - Does not collapse 'heterogeneous' security tools into a verb — they map per-tool, surfaced explicitly to avoid forced collapse.
  - Does not address whether route (derive, route) is truly status-class or wants its own slot. Initial proposal puts it under status; ready to revisit if usage shows otherwise.

DECISION POINTS FOR ANTHONY:

  (a) Name: toolkit_grammar() vs three_verbs() vs verbs(). I prefer toolkit_grammar — it names the artifact (a grammar over the toolkit) rather than the count.
  (b) Whether to expose sub-classes in the boot-context shape or hide them behind verb=<x> drill-down. My proposal: expose at top level for the discovery use case; the boot block is still small (3 verbs × ~5 lines = 15 lines + modifiers).
  (c) Whether 'heterogeneous' is the right shape for security or whether per-tool verb tagging is cleaner. I lean heterogeneous as an explicit category — forcing every tool into a verb creates pressure to over-collapse.

This is the sketch. Implementation belongs to the Stack-side instance (HQ Claude Code) when Anthony fires it. From here it's an architectural decision, not a coding ask.
